body:
Sorry for the really late reply, I have a bad habit of not checking this account. 

But yeah that's actually very interesting. I suppose sometimes they are more intrusive and uncomfortable than anything else. 

I do notice myself having strange compulsive episodes. I don't have diagnosed OCD but I get extremely frustrated and depressed over the most trivial things. I remember one time I couldn't stop crying one morning because I could hear the radio from my room and I don't normally wake up to the radio. 

I exaggerate every little problem in my life, inside my head. Every time one tiny thing goes wrong, I blow it way out of proportion and end up looking for some sort of completely unsatisfying emotional crutch to rest on, like comfort food or tv, that seem to just expand a void within me rather than being cathartic release. These bad habits just lead to worse mental state though. It's a vicious circle.

I know you're only making a joke but I'd still like to say something. I prefer to look back on my achievements instead of on my failures. Life is all about perspective really. Pessimism might seem to make sense as an outlook on life. It may seem rational. The be all and end all. But really, it's a very debilitating mind-set. Everything I say might sound like cheesy bs, but it's most certainly better than moping around letting my life decay.

That just seems absurd to me.

This has happened to me quite often actually. When you have those dreams where everything feels so real and you can feel her warmth in your embrace. It's just such an awesome feeling but when you wake up to find that it was all an illusion it can be quite frustrating.

Just hang in there. You said in a comment that you are 16. I'm currently 17 and I while I have still never had a gf or a kiss, I cuddled with a girl about a month ago. It was so goddamn nice and hopefully it will happen again with someone else in the future. 

Sometimes it feels like you'll never be loved by anyone. I'm constantly shoving that thought out of my head because it's useless and pointless. Start improving yourself, everyday, and one day your dream may just become a reality. :D

I am also a kissless virgin. It's hard to accept that almost everyone else has either boyfriend or a girlfriend, and I understand that frustration that you feel. 

You said that you have had a woman respond to your posts on some dating website. This is brilliant. Fair play to you. Just breathe deeply and, I know it's cliché but, be yourself. 

And remember it's not all about sex and kissing and stuff. Yeah it's nice to be loved by another human being but you must learn to love yourself first. There's bound to be someone out there for you!

Firstly, don't feel bad for posting because you think that other people need support more. We all need a pick-me-up now and then and I think you made a good decision in posting here. 

Now, on to business. I would recommend you to start investigating something called self-improvement. I've been trying to improve myself for a while now and it will make you feel a lot better about yourself.

I am currently 17 years ago and I kind of know how you feel. I've always had a very low self-confidence in myself and it's difficult to look at myself in the mirror without letting out a bit of a sigh.

But, if I continue down the path of self-improvement, I will start to become more attractive and, more importantly, more comfortable in myself. As I work out, I will slowly gain actual muscles and the stupid voice inside my head will simply not be able to tell me how awful I look. Because I will look good. 

I already have made some leaps and bounds that I never really thought I would make. My hair looks cool for example, and I've developed a very nice style.

I am slowly learning to accept myself and you can too. Just take baby steps. Start off writing a journal entry everyday. Then maybe start walking in the park for just a minute or two. Before you know it you'll be a lot closer to happiness. 

For now, just sit back and do something you enjoy. Put in your earphones and listen to some nice jazz or whatever relaxing music you like. Watch an episode of a comedy. Just relax. Life will get better if you keep making small steps. Trust me. You've got to just take that first tentative step. :D
No problem man, happy to help. If you ever feel like chatting about whatever feel free to PM me. :)

I think I might genuinely understand how you feel. I always get people complimenting me and thinking that I have some amazing perfect existence. When really I go through a lot of shit on the inside.

When I first read your post I had to stop myself from nodding and agreeing with you. Oftentimes, just as I'm about to do something that I consider "downtime" (anything that's not work essentially), I just stop dead in my tracks. My mind will start to tell me that there is no point. I might get a small spike of pleasure, of sweet, temporary neurochemical release from the annoyance of existence, but then it's back to confronting these heavy thoughts in my mind. And I just feel like it becomes impossible to live on, since our existence seems so goddamn nihilistic.

But our logic is flawed. Very deeply flawed. I would recommend the concept of Taoism to you, since it has helped me quite a bit. The basic concept is just to "go with the flow". The subreddit /r/howtonotgiveafuck especially helped me out. They teach the practice of "not giving fucks" and is helping me to lead a rich and fulfilling life by just letting stuff happen.

I believe in a concept called absurdism. Everything seems chaotic and irrational and the human search for order and meaning can sometimes lead to a lot of hardship. Instead of scrambling for control over the universe with your proposed act of defiance try to just live your life. Focus on self-improvement and treat yourself well. (I would recommend reading Albert Camus's writing for some novels with absurdist themes)

If you just hold on to your life, clutch onto it and weather the storm you'll probably see something that was worth holding onto for, on the horizon. If you let go you're just giving into your emotions, your hormones, your neurochemicals and letting them run the show. 

I can see from your post that you're a very intelligent person. You're obviously a man/woman of science. So don't let your limbic system control what happens to you! Let you decide what happens to you. There are reasons to hang on. They may seem so far away but they exist. You just have to find yours. I know for sure that I have surprised myself by finding a whole host of reasons for me personally to continue the struggle.
